anyOf.description: The claim must equal (or, for array claims, contain) this value.
The claim must equal (or, for array claims, contain) at least one of these values.

BoundClaimExpect.description: Expected value(s) for one bound claim: a single string, or a list matched as any-of.

OidcLogin.description: The OAuth client the gateway signs users in with at this identity provider, for MCP clients that present no gateway credential.

client_id.description: Client identifier registered at the identity provider. Its redirect URI is the gateway's public address followed by `/mcp-oauth/login/callback`.

client_secret.description: Client secret, sent to the token endpoint in the request body. Omit it for a public client.

scopes.description: Scopes to request beside `openid` and the provider's `required_scopes`.

audiences.description:
Accepted `aud` values. The token's audience (a string or an array) must contain at least one of these. Required unless `hmac_secret` is set; when a shared-secret provider omits it, the `aud` claim is ignored.

An empty list means exactly what omitting the field means — it carries no `minItems`, deliberately. The runtime reads "no accepted audiences" off `is_empty()`, so a schema that rejected `[]` would make the two planes disagree about what an empty list means and kill the whole row over a projection that spelled "unset" the other way. What stays rejected is a JWKS provider with no audiences at all, which `validate_semantics` owns.

bound_claims.description: Additional claim requirements, all of which must hold. Keys name claims (read as one claim of exactly that name, then with dots traversing nested objects, e.g. `"realm_access.roles"`); each requirement is satisfied when the claim equals — or, for array claims, contains — one of the expected values.

enabled.description: Whether the provider participates in JWT authentication. A disabled provider is kept but ignored. Treated as `true` when omitted.

hmac_secret.description: Shared secret for HMAC-signed tokens, whose presence selects HMAC verification for this provider. Its UTF-8 bytes are the HMAC key as-is — nothing is base64-decoded or derived — and it must be at least 32 bytes long. Tokens are then accepted only under `HS256`, `HS384` or `HS512`, no signing keys are fetched, and `issuer` / `audiences` become optional. Omit it for a standard OIDC provider whose tokens are verified against a JWKS.

identity_claim.description: Claim whose value selects the API key to act as: the request is bound to the key whose `jwt_subject` equals this claim's value. The value is first read as one claim of exactly this name, then with dots traversing nested objects (e.g. `"resource_access.account"`). Defaults to `sub`.

issuer.description: Expected `iss` claim, compared byte-for-byte against the token's issuer. A JWT carrying this issuer is verified against this provider and no other. Required unless `hmac_secret` is set; when a shared-secret provider omits it, the token's `iss` claim is not consulted at all.

jwks_uri.description: JWKS endpoint URL the signing keys are fetched from. When omitted, the endpoint is resolved once from the issuer's OIDC discovery document (`<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`) and cached. Must be absent when `hmac_secret` is set — a shared-secret provider fetches no keys.

leeway_secs.description: Clock-skew allowance in seconds applied to time-based claims (`exp`, `nbf`). Defaults to 0.

login.description: Signs users in at this provider when they connect an MCP client with no gateway credential to an MCP server with `auth_type: oauth2_authorization_code`. When exactly one enabled provider in the environment has it, every such server uses this sign-in; when none does, those servers keep relaying the client's sign-in and need a gateway credential. Usable only on an enabled provider with `issuer` and no `hmac_secret`, whose endpoints come from the issuer's OIDC discovery document. A second enabled provider with it, or one on a provider that cannot use it, makes sign-in fail with `mcp_oauth_misconfigured`. The gateway checks the ID token's audience against `client_id`, so `audiences` need not list it.

name.description: Human-readable provider name, unique within the environment (e.g. `"corp-keycloak"`).

required_scopes.description: Scopes that must all be present in the token's `scope` claim (a space-delimited string or an array of strings). An empty list requires nothing.

tag_claims.description:
Cost-attribution tags read from the verified token, as tag key to claim path — for example `{"department": "department", "subsidiary": "org.subsidiary"}`. For each request this provider authenticates, the value a path yields takes precedence, per tag key, over the `tags` of the API key, its team and its member; a session from an MCP client's sign-in reads the claims recorded at sign-in. The token is not written back to any of those documents.

A path is first read as one claim of exactly that name, then with dots traversing nested objects. A string is used as is and a number as its JSON text. An array of strings and numbers becomes its distinct values, sorted and joined with commas. Any other value, an empty array, or a value, array element or joined result that is not 1 to 128 characters, contains a control character, or starts or ends with whitespace yields nothing, and the tag key keeps the value the API key, team or member gives it.

Keys match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$`, paths are non-empty, and at most 32 entries are allowed. Omitted or empty means tags are not read from tokens.
